units.zh: 列傳一百三十八
units.en: Biographies 138
units.literal: Biographies 138

units.zh: 沈初金士松鄒炳泰戴聯奎王懿修子宗誠黃鉞
units.en: Shen Chu, Jin Shisong, Zou Bingtai, Dai Liankui, Wang Yixiu (and his son Zong Cheng), and Huang Yue
units.literal: Shen Chu, Jin Shisong, Zou Bingtai, Dai Liankui, Wang Yixiu, son Zong Cheng, Huang Yue

units.zh: 沈初，字景初，浙江平湖人。
units.en: Shen Chu, courtesy name Jingchu, came from Pinghu in Zhejiang.
units.literal: Shen Chu, style name Jingchu, was a native of Pinghu, Zhejiang.

units.zh: 少有異禀，讀書目數行下，同郡錢陳群稱為異才。
units.en: As a boy he showed unusual talent and could read several lines at a glance; Qian Chenqun of his prefecture hailed him as a prodigy.
units.literal: In youth he possessed unusual gifts; when reading, his eye took in several lines at once; Qian Chenqun of the same commandery called him a prodigy.

units.zh: 乾隆二十七年，南巡，召試，賜舉人，授內閣中書。
units.en: In Qianlong 27, during the emperor's southern tour, he was summoned for a special examination, granted the rank of provincial graduate, and appointed drafter in the Grand Secretariat.
units.literal: In the 27th year of Qianlong, during the southern tour, he was summoned for examination, granted juren status, and appointed a Secretariat drafter in the Grand Secretariat.

units.zh: 明年，成一甲第三名進士，授編修。
units.en: The following year he finished third in the jinshi examinations and was appointed a Hanlin compiler.
units.literal: The next year, he placed third in the first class of jinshi, and was appointed compiler.

units.zh: 三十二年，直懋勤殿，合寫經為皇太后祝釐。
units.en: In Qianlong 32 he served in the Hall of Assiduous Cultivation, copying scriptures with others to invoke blessings for the empress dowager.
units.literal: In the 32nd year, he was assigned to the Maoqin Hall, where he joined others in copying sutras to pray for blessings for the Empress Dowager.

units.zh: 逾年，大考翰詹，以直內廷未與試，詔褒初學問優美，特晉一秩，擢侍講。
units.en: When the Hanlin triennial examinations came around, he was exempted because he was serving in the inner palace; the emperor commended his scholarship and promoted him one rank to Reader-in-Waiting.
units.literal: The following year, in the triennial examination of Hanlin and Hanlin Bachelors, because he was on duty in the inner court he did not take part in the test; an edict praised Chu's excellent learning and specially promoted him one rank, appointing him Reader-in-Waiting.

units.zh: 三十六年，直南書房，督河南學政，未赴任，丁祖母承重憂。
units.en: In Qianlong 36 he served in the Southern Library and was named Henan educational commissioner, but before he could take up the post he went into mourning for his grandmother.
units.literal: In the 36th year, he was assigned to the Southern Library; he was appointed educational commissioner of Henan but before taking up the post entered mourning for his paternal grandmother, bearing the heaviest obligations of filial mourning.

units.zh: 服闋，遷右庶子。
units.en: After mourning he was made Right Vice Supervisor of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: When mourning ended, he was transferred to Right Vice Supervisor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 累擢禮部侍郎，督福建學政。
units.en: He rose to Vice Minister of Rites and served as Fujian's educational commissioner.
units.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of Rites and served as educational commissioner of Fujian.

units.zh: 遭本生父憂，服闋，起兵部侍郎。
units.en: After mourning his biological father he returned to office as Vice Minister of War.
units.literal: He suffered mourning for his biological father; when mourning ended, he took up the post of Vice Minister of War.

units.zh: 尋以母病乞歸終養。
units.en: He soon petitioned to retire home to care for his ailing mother until her death.
units.literal: Soon afterward, because of his mother's illness, he requested leave to return home for final care.

units.zh: 後起故官，督順天學政，調江蘇。
units.en: Later recalled, he served as Shuntian educational commissioner and then was transferred to Jiangsu.
units.literal: Later he was recalled to his former office, served as educational commissioner of Shuntian, and was transferred to Jiangsu.

units.zh: 任滿回京，調吏部，又督江西學政。
units.en: After his term he returned to the capital, moved to the Board of Civil Appointments, and later served as Jiangxi educational commissioner.
units.literal: When his term ended he returned to the capital, was transferred to the Board of Civil Appointments, and again served as educational commissioner of Jiangxi.

units.zh: 初以文學受知，歷充四庫全書館、三通館副總裁，續編石渠寶笈、秘殿珠林，校勘太學石經。
units.en: Known for his scholarship, he served as deputy chief compiler for the Complete Library of the Four Treasuries and the Comprehensive Administrative Codes projects, helped continue the imperial art catalogues, and collated the academy stone classics.
units.literal: Chu had gained recognition for his literary scholarship; he served in succession as vice director-general of the Siku Quanshu Project and the Santong Project, continued compilation of the Shiqu Baoji and the Midian Zhulin, and collated the Stone Classics of the Imperial Academy.

units.zh: 嘉慶元年，與千叟宴，充會試知貢舉。
units.en: In Jiaqing 1 he attended the Thousand Elders Banquet and presided over the metropolitan examinations.
units.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, he attended the Banquet for a Thousand Elders and served as director of the metropolitan examination.

units.zh: 擢左都御史，授軍機大臣，遷兵部尚書，歷吏、戶二部。
units.en: He was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief and Grand Councillor, served as Minister of War, and later held the Civil Appointments and Revenue portfolios.
units.literal: He was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief, appointed Grand Councillor, transferred to Minister of War, and served in the Boards of Civil Appointments and Revenue in succession.

units.zh: 四年，以老罷樞務，免直內廷，充實錄館副總裁。
units.en: In Jiaqing 4, on grounds of age he left the Grand Council and inner-court service and became deputy chief compiler of the Veritable Records.
units.literal: In the fourth year, because of age he was relieved of Grand Council duties, released from inner-court assignment, and appointed vice director-general of the Veritable Records Project.

units.zh: 未幾卒，諡文恪，祀賢良祠。
units.en: He died soon afterward and was posthumously titled Wenge and honored in the Temple of Worthies.
units.literal: Before long he died; posthumous title Wenge; enshrined in the Temple of Worthies.

units.zh: 金士松，字亭立，江蘇吳江人，寄籍宛平。
units.en: Jin Shisong, courtesy name Tingli, was from Wujiang in Jiangsu but registered his domicile at Wanping.
units.literal: Jin Shisong, style name Tingli, was a native of Wujiang, Jiangsu, with registered domicile at Wanping.

units.zh: 舉順天鄉試，改歸原籍。
units.en: After passing the metropolitan provincial exam he reverted his registration to his native prefecture.
units.literal: He passed the Shuntian provincial examination and then changed back to his original domicile.

units.zh: 乾隆二十五年，成進士，選庶吉士，授編修。
units.en: In Qianlong 25 he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
units.literal: In the 25th year of Qianlong, he became a jinshi, was selected as Hanlin Bachelor, and appointed compiler.

units.zh: 遷侍讀，直懋勤殿寫經。
units.en: He was promoted to Reader and assigned to copy scriptures in the Hall of Assiduous Cultivation.
units.literal: He was transferred to Reader, assigned to the Maojin Hall to copy scriptures.

units.zh: 典福建鄉試，督廣東學政。
units.en: He presided over the Fujian provincial exams and served as Guangdong educational commissioner.
units.literal: He presided over the Fujian provincial examination and served as educational commissioner of Guangdong.

units.zh: 直南書房，累遷詹事，以生母憂歸。
units.en: After serving in the Southern Library and rising to Grand Tutor, he went home to mourn his birth mother.
units.literal: He was assigned to the Southern Library, was promoted in succession to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and returned home on mourning for his birth mother.

units.zh: 服闋，會高宗南巡，迎鑾道左，回京督順天學政。
units.en: After mourning he greeted the Qianlong Emperor during a southern tour and, on returning to Beijing, took charge of Shuntian education.
units.literal: When mourning ended, it coincided with the Gaozong Emperor's southern tour; he welcomed the imperial procession on the roadside; returning to the capital he served as educational commissioner of Shuntian.

units.zh: 以寄籍辭，詔免迴避，聯任凡七年。
units.en: He tried to decline because of domicile rules, but the emperor waived the conflict-of-interest requirement and let him serve seven years straight.
units.literal: He declined on grounds of domicile registration; an edict exempted him from the avoidance rule, and he held the post consecutively for seven years in all.

units.zh: 累擢禮部侍郎，調兵部。
units.en: He rose to Vice Minister of Rites and was then transferred to War.
units.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of Rites and transferred to the Ministry of War.

units.zh: 五十年，帝御乾清宮，賜千叟宴。
units.en: In Qianlong 50 the emperor held the Thousand Elders Banquet in the Palace of Heavenly Purity.
units.literal: In the 50th year, the Emperor held court at the Palace of Heavenly Purity and granted a Banquet for a Thousand Elders.

units.zh: 士松年五十七，未得與，特命試詩，賞賚同一品。
units.en: At fifty-seven he was too young for the banquet, but the emperor had him compose a poem and rewarded him as if he ranked among the guests.
units.literal: Shisong was fifty-seven and did not qualify to attend; he was specially ordered to submit a poem for examination, and rewards were granted equal to those of the first rank.

units.zh: 調吏部，直講經筵，校勘石經，遷左都御史。
units.en: He moved to Civil Appointments, lectured at the imperial classics sessions, collated the stone classics, and became Left Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: He was transferred to the Board of Civil Appointments, lectured at the Classic Lectures, collated the Stone Classics, and was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 嘉慶元年，再與千叟宴，遷禮部尚書。
units.en: In Jiaqing 1 he attended the Thousand Elders Banquet again and was promoted to Minister of Rites.
units.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, he again attended the Thousand Elders Banquet and was promoted to Minister of Rites.

units.zh: 二年，調兵部，罷直書房。
units.en: In Jiaqing 2 he was moved to War and released from library duty.
units.literal: In the second year, he was transferred to the Ministry of War and dismissed from duty in the Library.

units.zh: 五年，扈蹕謁裕陵，途次嬰疾，遣御醫診視。
units.en: In Jiaqing 5, on the way to pay respects at the Yuling Mausoleum, he fell ill and the emperor sent a court physician.
units.literal: In the fifth year, while accompanying the imperial procession to visit the Yuling Mausoleum, he fell ill en route and the emperor sent an imperial physician to examine him.

units.zh: 還京，卒，諡文簡，祀賢良祠。
units.en: He died after returning to Beijing, was posthumously titled Wenjian, and honored in the Temple of Worthies.
units.literal: Returning to the capital, he died; posthumous title Wenjian; enshrined in the Temple of Worthies.

units.zh: 鄒炳泰，字仲文，江蘇無錫人。
units.en: Zou Bingtai, courtesy name Zhongwen, was from Wuxi in Jiangsu.
units.literal: Zou Bingtai, style name Zhongwen, was a native of Wuxi, Jiangsu.

units.zh: 乾隆三十七年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，纂修四庫全書，遷國子監司業。
units.en: A jinshi of Qianlong 37, he entered the Hanlin, served as compiler on the Complete Library project, and rose to Vice Director of the Imperial Academy.
units.literal: Jinshi in the 37th year of Qianlong, selected Hanlin Bachelor, appointed compiler, compiled the Siku Quanshu, promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Academy.

units.zh: 國學因元、明舊，未立辟雍，炳泰援古制疏請。
units.en: The academy still followed Yuan and Ming models and lacked a ceremonial hall; Bingtai memorialized citing ancient precedent.
units.literal: The Imperial Academy followed Yuan and Ming precedent and had no Piyong Hall; Bingtai cited ancient rites in a memorial requesting one.

units.zh: 四十八年，高宗釋奠禮成，因下詔增建辟雍。
units.en: In Qianlong 48, after the emperor's ceremonial offerings at the academy, he ordered construction of the Hall of the Circular Moat.
units.literal: In the 48th year, after the Gaozong Emperor completed the sacrifice and libation rites, he issued an edict ordering the addition of a Piyong Hall.

units.zh: 逾兩年，始舉臨雍禮，稱盛典焉。
units.en: Two years later the emperor presided at the academy for the first time—a ceremony hailed as grand indeed.
units.literal: More than two years later, the Emperor's visit to the Academy rite was first performed, and it was hailed as a great ceremony.

units.zh: 尋超擢炳泰為祭酒。
units.en: Bingtai was soon promoted ahead of schedule to Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.
units.literal: Soon afterward Bingtai was exceptionally promoted to Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.

units.zh: 累遷內閣學士，歷山東、江西學政。
units.en: He rose to Grand Secretariat academician and served as educational commissioner in Shandong and Jiangxi.
units.literal: He was promoted in succession to Grand Secretariat Academician and served as educational commissioner of Shandong and Jiangxi.

units.zh: 嘉慶四年，授禮部侍郎，調倉場，剔除積弊。
units.en: In Jiaqing 4 he became Vice Minister of Rites, took charge of the granaries, and cleared away long-standing corruption.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing, he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites, transferred to granary administration, and eliminated longstanding abuses.

units.zh: 坐糧廳顏培天不職，劾去之。
units.en: He impeached Yan Peitian of the grain office for neglect of duty and had him removed.
units.literal: Because Yan Peitian of the grain office was derelict in duty, he impeached and had him removed.

units.zh: 六年，京察，特予議敘。
units.en: In Jiaqing 6 the capital personnel review singled him out for commendation.
units.literal: In the sixth year, at the capital evaluation, he was specially granted consideration for reward and promotion.

units.zh: 軍船交糧掛欠，已許抵補，後至者復然。
units.en: Transport boats that delivered short were allowed to make up the deficit—and later arrivals did the same.
units.literal: When military transport boats delivered grain with deficits on account, offset was already permitted; those arriving later did the same again.

units.zh: 炳泰慮年年積欠，與同官達慶意不合，自具疏奏，詔斥其偏執使氣，鐫級留任。
units.en: Fearing endless accumulated shortfalls, he clashed with colleague Da Qing and memorialized on his own; the emperor rebuked his obstinacy, demoted him one rank, but kept him in office.
units.literal: Bingtai feared annual accumulation of deficits; he did not agree with his colleague Da Qing; he submitted his own memorial; an edict rebuked him for obstinate temperament, stripped one rank, and kept him at his post.

units.zh: 又奏監督輪值宿倉，倉役出入滋弊，宜令於倉外官房居住，從之。
units.en: He also argued that supervisors sleeping inside the granaries invited graft and should live in the outside quarters—the emperor agreed.
units.literal: He also memorialized that supervisors took turns lodging in the granary, that entry and exit by granary servants fostered abuse, and that they ought to be ordered to reside in the official quarters outside the granary; the proposal was adopted.

units.zh: 十年，擢左都御史，遷兵部尚書，兼署工部，管理戶部三庫。
units.en: In Jiaqing 10 he became Left Censor-in-Chief and Minister of War, acted as Minister of Works, and supervised the three revenue treasuries.
units.literal: In the tenth year, promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief, transferred to Minister of War, concurrently acting Minister of Works, and managing the three treasuries of the Board of Revenue.

units.zh: 十一年，兼管順天府尹事。
units.en: In Jiaqing 11 he also oversaw the Shuntian prefect's office.
units.literal: In the eleventh year, he concurrently oversaw the affairs of the Shuntian prefect.

units.zh: 十二年，調吏部。
units.en: In Jiaqing 12 he was transferred to Civil Appointments.
units.literal: In the twelfth year, transferred to the Board of Civil Appointments.

units.zh: 十四年，加太子少保。
units.en: In Jiaqing 14 he received the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: In the fourteenth year, he was given the added title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 倉吏高添鳳盜米事覺，坐久任倉場無所覺察，褫宮銜，降二品頂戴，​​革職留任，久乃復之。
units.en: When granary clerk Gao Tianfeng's theft came to light, Bingtai was blamed for failing to detect it during his long tenure; he lost his honorific rank and second-rank insignia, was dismissed but kept on, and eventually had them restored.
units.literal: When the theft of grain by granary clerk Gao Tianfeng was discovered, he was held responsible for long service in granary administration without detection; his palace rank was stripped, he was demoted to second-rank insignia, dismissed from office but retained at his post, and only after a long time was it restored.

units.zh: 十六年，署戶部尚書。
units.en: In Jiaqing 16 he acted as Minister of Revenue.
units.literal: In the sixteenth year, acting Minister of Revenue.

units.zh: 尋以吏部尚書協辦大學士。
units.en: He soon served as Associate Grand Secretary while holding the Civil Appointments portfolio.
units.literal: Soon afterward, as Minister of Civil Appointments he served as Associate Grand Secretary.

units.zh: 炳泰在吏部久，尤慎銓政。
units.en: Bingtai had long served at Civil Appointments and was famously meticulous about personnel decisions.
units.literal: Bingtai served long in the Board of Civil Appointments and was especially careful in appointment matters.

units.zh: 十八年，銓選兵部主事有誤，同官瑚圖禮徇司員議，回護堅執。
units.en: In Jiaqing 18 a War Ministry appointment went wrong; colleague Hutuli sided with the staff and refused to back down.
units.literal: In the eighteenth year, there was an error in the selection of a secretary in the Ministry of War; colleague Hutuli indulged the departmental staff's opinion and stubbornly shielded them.

units.zh: 炳泰力爭曰：「吾年已衰，何戀戀祿位？
units.en: Bingtai protested: "I am old—why should I cling to rank and salary?
units.literal: Bingtai argued forcefully: "I am already old in years—why should I cling so to salary and rank?

units.zh: 不可使朝廷法自我壞！」
units.en: I cannot be the one to break the court's law!"
units.literal: One must not let the laws of the court be broken starting with me!"

units.zh: 自具疏白其故，上韙其言，卒罷瑚圖禮。
units.en: He memorialized the emperor himself; the emperor approved, and Hutuli was dismissed.
units.literal: He submitted his own memorial explaining the reason; the Emperor approved his words, and Hutuli was finally dismissed.

units.zh: 既而有降革官捐复者二人，準駁不當，侍郎初彭齡論與不合，疏聞，上斥炳泰無定見，鐫級留任。
units.en: Later he mishandled two demoted officials seeking reinstatement by purchase; Vice Minister Chu Pengling disagreed, and the emperor rebuked Bingtai's inconsistency, demoted him one rank, and kept him on.
units.literal: Afterward there were two dismissed officials who purchased restoration; approval and rejection were improper; Vice Minister Chu Pengling's opinion differed; when the memorial reached the throne, the Emperor rebuked Bingtai for lack of fixed judgment, stripped one rank, and kept him at his post.

units.zh: 又盜劫兵部主事姚堃於昌平八仙莊，詔以地近京畿，官吏闒茸，不能治盜，罷炳泰兼管府尹事。
units.en: When bandits robbed War Ministry secretary Yao Kun near Changping, the emperor blamed local incompetence so close to the capital and stripped Bingtai of his concurrent prefectural duties.
units.literal: Also, Secretary Yao Kun of the Ministry of War was robbed by bandits at Baxian Village in Changping; an edict held that the place was near the capital region, officials were negligent, and bandits could not be suppressed; Bingtai was removed from concurrent oversight of the prefect's affairs.

units.zh: 及教匪林清變起，逆黨多居固安及黃村，追論炳泰在官不能覺察，以中允、贊善降補。
units.en: When Lin Qing's sectarian rebellion broke out—many rebels lived in Gu'an and Huangcun—the court held that Bingtai should have known; he was demoted to middle academicianship and tutor.
units.literal: When the heterodox sect rebel Lin Qing's uprising erupted, many rebels lived in Gu'an and Huangcun; retrospectively it was held that Bingtai in office had failed to detect them; he was demoted and reassigned as Academician Expositor and Mentor.

units.zh: 尋休致，歸。
units.en: He soon retired and went home.
units.literal: Soon he retired and returned home.

units.zh: 二十五年，卒。
units.en: He died in Jiaqing 25.
units.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, he died.

units.zh: 柄泰自初登第，不登權要之門，浮沉館職，久之始躋卿貳。
units.en: From his first degree onward Bingtai never cultivated powerful patrons; he lingered in Hanlin posts long before reaching vice-ministerial rank.
units.literal: From first passing the examinations, Bingtai did not visit the doors of the powerful; he drifted in Hanlin posts and only after long years reached vice-ministerial rank.

units.zh: 屢掌文衡，稱得士。
units.en: He presided over many examinations and was known for finding talent.
units.literal: He repeatedly presided over literary examinations and was praised for selecting worthy men.

units.zh: 立朝不苟，仁宗重之，而終黜。
units.en: He was upright in office and valued by the Jiaqing Emperor, yet was ultimately dismissed.
units.literal: In court he was not lax; the Jiaqing Emperor valued him, yet in the end he was dismissed.

units.zh: 戴聯奎，字紫垣，江蘇如皋人。
units.en: Dai Liankui, courtesy name Ziyuan, was from Rugao in Jiangsu.
units.literal: Dai Liankui, style name Ziyuan, was a native of Rugao, Jiangsu.

units.zh: 乾隆四十年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。
units.en: A jinshi of Qianlong 40, he entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor and was appointed compiler.
units.literal: Jinshi in the 40th year of Qianlong, selected Hanlin Bachelor, appointed compiler.

units.zh: 聯奎少從邵晉涵受經學，既通籍，以清節自厲，在翰林久不遷。
units.en: Liankui studied classics under Shao Jinhan as a youth; once in office he held himself to strict integrity and lingered in the Hanlin without advancement.
units.literal: Liankui in youth studied the classics under Shao Jinhan; after entering official service he upheld integrity and remained long in the Hanlin without promotion.

units.zh: 大學士嵇璜掌院事，將保送御史，列聯奎名，滿掌院學士曰：「吾未識其人，何以論其才否？」
units.en: When Grand Secretary Ji Huang, as academy chief, listed Liankui among censor nominees, the Manchu chancellor objected: "I do not know him—how can I judge his ability?"
units.literal: Grand Secretary Ji Huang was in charge of the Academy; he was about to recommend censors for appointment and listed Liankui's name; the Manchu Chancellor of the Academy said: "I do not know the man—how can I judge whether he has talent or not?"

units.zh: 璜以語聯奎，使往見，聯奎漫應之，不往。
units.en: Ji Huang told Liankui to call on the chancellor; Liankui gave a vague reply and never went.
units.literal: Huang told Liankui and had him go to pay a visit; Liankui responded casually and did not go.

units.zh: 及京察舉一等，又列聯奎名，復言如前，終不得與，璜乃益重之。
units.en: At the next capital review he was again nominated, and the chancellor repeated the same objection; Liankui was passed over again, and Ji Huang respected him all the more.
units.literal: When the capital evaluation nominated first rank and again listed Liankui's name, the same words were spoken as before; in the end he did not obtain the appointment, and Huang only valued him the more.

units.zh: 和珅為掌院，訪時望傅其子丰紳殷德，或薦晉涵及聯奎，晉涵移病歸，聯奎亦堅辭。
units.en: When Heshen headed the academy he sought tutors for his son Fengshen Yinde; Shao Jinhan and Liankui were suggested, but Jinhan pleaded illness and went home and Liankui firmly refused.
units.literal: When Heshen was Chancellor, he sought men of reputation to tutor his son Fengshen Yinde; some recommended Jinhan and Liankui; Jinhan pleaded illness and returned home, and Liankui also firmly declined.

units.zh: 循資累遷至內閣學士。
units.en: He rose by seniority to Grand Secretariat academician.
units.literal: By seniority he was promoted in succession to Grand Secretariat Academician.

units.zh: 嘉慶九年，遷兵部侍郎，歷禮部、兵部、吏部。
units.en: In Jiaqing 9 he became Vice Minister of War and later served in Rites, War, and Civil Appointments.
units.literal: In the ninth year of Jiaqing, transferred to Vice Minister of War, and served in the Ministries of Rites, War, and Civil Appointments in succession.

units.zh: 二十一年，擢左都御史。
units.en: In Jiaqing 21 he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: In the twenty-first year, promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 逾年，擢禮部尚書，調兵部。
units.en: The next year he became Minister of Rites and was transferred to War.
units.literal: The following year, promoted to Minister of Rites, transferred to the Ministry of War.

units.zh: 二十五年，失行印，坐降三品京堂，補太常寺卿，督浙江學政。
units.en: In Jiaqing 25 he lost an official seal while traveling, was demoted to third rank, appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and sent as Zhejiang educational commissioner.
units.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, he lost the official seal on a journey; on that account he was demoted to third-rank capital official, appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and served as educational commissioner of Zhejiang.

units.zh: 道光元年，擢禮部侍郎，又擢兵部尚書。
units.en: In Daoguang 1 he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and then to Minister of War.
units.literal: In the first year of Daoguang, promoted to Vice Minister of Rites, and again promoted to Minister of War.

units.zh: 召還京，未至，卒。
units.en: He was recalled to the capital but died before he arrived.
units.literal: Summoned back to the capital, before arriving he died.

units.zh: 王懿修，字仲美，安徽青陽人。
units.en: Wang Yixiu, courtesy name Zhongmei, was from Qingyang in Anhui.
units.literal: Wang Yixiu, style name Zhongmei, was a native of Qingyang, Anhui.

units.zh: 乾隆三十一年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。
units.en: A jinshi of Qianlong 31, he entered the Hanlin as a bachelor and was appointed compiler.
units.literal: Jinshi in the 31st year of Qianlong, selected Hanlin Bachelor, appointed compiler.

units.zh: 入直上書房，授慶郡王永璘讀。
units.en: He served in the Upper Library as tutor to Prince Qing Yonglin.
units.literal: He entered service in the Upper Library and instructed Prince Qing, Yong Lin, in reading.

units.zh: 典陝西、廣東、江西鄉試，督廣西、湖北學政，洊擢少詹事。
units.en: He presided over provincial exams in Shaanxi, Guangdong, and Jiangxi, served as educational commissioner in Guangxi and Hubei, and rose to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: He presided over the provincial examinations of Shaanxi, Guangdong, and Jiangxi, served as educational commissioner of Guangxi and Hubei, and was promoted in succession to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 五十四年，引病歸，終父母喪始出，复乞病在告。
units.en: In Qianlong 54 he retired on grounds of illness; after completing mourning for both parents he briefly returned, then again took sick leave.
units.literal: In the 54th year, he pleaded illness and returned home; only after completing mourning for both parents did he emerge, and again requested leave on grounds of illness.

units.zh: 嘉慶元年，舉行千叟宴，懿修與焉，被御製詩刻、玉鳩杖、文綺之賜。
units.en: At the Jiaqing 1 Thousand Elders Banquet he received an inscribed imperial poem, a jade dove staff, and brocade.
units.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, when the Thousand Elders Banquet was held, Yixiu was among them and received gifts of an imperial poem carved on stone, a jade dove staff, and patterned silk.

units.zh: 七年，起授通政司副使，歷光祿寺卿、內閣學士。
units.en: In Jiaqing 7 he was recalled as Vice Commissioner of the Transmission Office and later served as Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and Grand Secretariat academician.
units.literal: In the seventh year, recalled and appointed Vice Commissioner of the Transmission Office, and served in succession as Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and Grand Secretariat Academician.

units.zh: 八年，擢禮部侍郎，督順天學政。
units.en: In Jiaqing 8 he became Vice Minister of Rites and Shuntian educational commissioner.
units.literal: In the eighth year, promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and served as educational commissioner of Shuntian.

units.zh: 十年，擢左都御史，回京供職。
units.en: In Jiaqing 10 he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief and returned to duty in the capital.
units.literal: In the tenth year, promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief and returned to the capital to serve.

units.zh: 尋擢禮部尚書，管戶部三庫事。
units.en: He was soon promoted to Minister of Rites and put in charge of the three revenue treasuries.
units.literal: Soon promoted to Minister of Rites and managed the three treasuries of the Board of Revenue.

units.zh: 十二年，充上書房總師傅。
units.en: In Jiaqing 12 he became Chief Tutor of the Upper Library.
units.literal: In the twelfth year, he served as Chief Tutor of the Upper Library.

units.zh: 十四年，萬壽慶典，加太子少保，典會試。
units.en: At the Jiaqing 14 longevity celebration he received the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and presided over the metropolitan examinations.
units.literal: In the fourteenth year, at the Longevity Celebration, he was given the added title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and presided over the metropolitan examination.

units.zh: 懿修持躬端謹，製作雅正，甚被仁宗眷遇。
units.en: Yixiu was upright and careful in conduct, wrote in an elegant and correct style, and enjoyed great favor from the Jiaqing Emperor.
units.literal: Yixiu conducted himself with upright caution; his compositions were elegant and correct; he was greatly favored by the Jiaqing Emperor.

units.zh: 十八年，以老致仕。
units.en: In Jiaqing 18 he retired on grounds of age.
units.literal: In the eighteenth year, he retired on grounds of age.

units.zh: 逾二年，年八十，賜壽，謁宮門謝，逢上出禦經筵，親解佩囊賜之。
units.en: Two years later, on his eightieth birthday, he came to the palace to give thanks for the imperial birthday gift; the emperor, on his way to the classics lecture, personally took off his purse and gave it to him.
units.literal: More than two years later, at age eighty, longevity was granted; he came to the palace gate to give thanks; he encountered the Emperor coming out to preside at the Classic Lectures and personally unfastened his purse-pouch and bestowed it on him.

units.zh: 二十一年，卒。
units.en: He died in Jiaqing 21.
units.literal: In the twenty-first year, he died.

units.zh: 諡文僖。
units.en: He was posthumously titled Wenxi.
units.literal: Posthumous title Wenxi.

units.zh: 子宗誠，字廉甫。
units.en: His son Zong Cheng, courtesy name Lianfu.
units.literal: His son Zong Cheng, style name Lianfu.

units.zh: 乾隆五十五年一甲三名進士，授編修。
units.en: In Qianlong 55 he placed third in the jinshi examinations and was appointed a Hanlin compiler.
units.literal: In the 55th year of Qianlong, third in the first class of jinshi, appointed compiler.

units.zh: 嘉慶中，歷典雲南、四川、陝西鄉試，督河南、山東、江西學政，洊擢禮部侍郎，歷工部、兵部，典會試。
units.en: Under Jiaqing he presided over provincial exams in Yunnan, Sichuan, and Shaanxi, served as educational commissioner in Henan, Shandong, and Jiangxi, rose to Vice Minister of Rites, held posts in Works and War, and presided over the metropolitan examinations.
units.literal: During the Jiaqing reign, he presided in succession over the provincial examinations of Yunnan, Sichuan, and Shaanxi, served as educational commissioner of Henan, Shandong, and Jiangxi, was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of Rites, served in the Ministries of Works and War, and presided over the metropolitan examination.

units.zh: 道光二年，擢兵部尚書，歷署禮部、工部尚書，兼管順天府尹。
units.en: In Daoguang 2 he became Minister of War, acted as Minister of Rites and Minister of Works, and also oversaw the Shuntian prefect's office.
units.literal: In the second year of Daoguang, promoted to Minister of War, served in succession as acting Minister of Rites and Minister of Works, and concurrently oversaw the Shuntian prefect.

units.zh: 當懿修為侍郎時，宗誠已官學士，尋隨父扈蹕東巡，侍宴翰林院，父子同席。
units.en: While Yixiu was a vice minister, Zong Cheng was already an academician; he later joined his father on an eastern tour and, at a Hanlin banquet, father and son sat at the same table.
units.literal: When Yixiu was Vice Minister, Zong Cheng already held the rank of Academician; soon afterward he accompanied his father on the eastern tour in the imperial retinue, attended a banquet at the Hanlin Academy, and father and son shared the same seat.

units.zh: 高宗實錄成，賜宴禮部，懿修以尚書主席。
units.en: When the Qianlong Veritable Records were completed, the court held a banquet at the Ministry of Rites with Yixiu, as minister, presiding.
units.literal: When the Veritable Records of the Gaozong Emperor were completed, a banquet was granted at the Ministry of Rites; Yixiu as Minister presided.

units.zh: 懿修致仕後，宗誠繼直上書房，海內推為榮遇。
units.en: After Yixiu retired, Zong Cheng continued in the Upper Library—a succession widely hailed as a great honor.
units.literal: After Yixiu retired, Zong Cheng continued service in the Upper Library; throughout the realm this was acclaimed as a signal honor.

units.zh: 上亦以其兩世官禁近，皆能清慎，特優睞焉。
units.en: The emperor also favored them specially, noting that for two generations they had served close to the throne with integrity and discretion.
units.literal: The Emperor also, because for two generations they had held posts near the throne and both were able to be pure and cautious, showed them special favor.

units.zh: 道光十七年，卒。
units.en: He died in Daoguang 17.
units.literal: In the seventeenth year of Daoguang, he died.

units.zh: 黃鉞，字左田，安徽當塗人。
units.en: Huang Yue, courtesy name Zuotian, was from Dangtu in Anhui.
units.literal: Huang Yue, style name Zuotian, was a native of Dangtu, Anhui.

units.zh: 乾隆五十五年進士，授戶部主事。
units.en: A jinshi of Qianlong 55, he was appointed a secretary in the Board of Revenue.
units.literal: Jinshi in the 55th year of Qianlong, appointed secretary in the Board of Revenue.

units.zh: 時和珅管部務，鉞不欲趨附，乞假歸，不出。
units.en: Heshen then controlled the ministry; Yue refused to court him, took leave, went home, and stayed out of office.
units.literal: At the time Heshen managed the ministry's affairs; Yue did not wish to curry favor, requested leave to return home, and did not come out.

units.zh: 嘉慶四年，仁宗親政，硃珪薦之，召來京。
units.en: In Jiaqing 4, when the emperor took direct rule, Zhu Gui recommended him and he was summoned to Beijing.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing, when the Jiaqing Emperor took personal rule, Zhu Gui recommended him and he was summoned to the capital.

units.zh: 入見，上曰：「朕居籓邸時，知汝名久矣，何以假歸不出？」
units.en: At audience the emperor said: "When I was still a prince I had long known your name—why did you take leave and stay away?"
units.literal: On entering audience, the Emperor said: "When I resided in the princely mansion, I knew your name long ago—why did you take leave and not come out?"

units.zh: 鉞以實對，荷溫諭，尋直懋勤殿。
units.en: Yue answered frankly, received a warm response, and was soon assigned to the Hall of Assiduous Cultivation.
units.literal: Yue answered truthfully, received a gracious edict, and soon was assigned to the Maojin Hall.

units.zh: 九年，改贊善，入直南書房，未補官，命與考試差，典山東鄉試。
units.en: In Jiaqing 9 he became a mentor, entered the Southern Library, and before a regular post was confirmed was sent to preside over the Shandong provincial exams.
units.literal: In the ninth year, transferred to Mentor, entered duty in the Southern Library; before his post was filled, he was ordered to take examination assignments and presided over the Shandong provincial examination.

units.zh: 十年，督山西學政，累遷庶子。
units.en: In Jiaqing 10 he served as Shanxi educational commissioner and rose to Vice Supervisor of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: In the tenth year, served as educational commissioner of Shanxi, promoted in succession to Vice Supervisor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 十五年，差滿，仍直南書房，遷侍講學士。
units.en: In Jiaqing 15, when his term ended, he returned to the Southern Library and was promoted to Reader and Academician.
units.literal: In the fifteenth year, when his assignment ended, he still served in the Southern Library and was transferred to Reader and Academician.

units.zh: 十八年，复典山東鄉試，留學政，擢內閣學士。
units.en: In Jiaqing 18 he again presided over the Shandong provincial exams, stayed on as educational commissioner, and was promoted to Grand Secretariat academician.
units.literal: In the eighteenth year, again presided over the Shandong provincial examination, remained as educational commissioner, and was promoted to Grand Secretariat Academician.

units.zh: 是年，滑縣教匪起，蔓延山東，劾罷失察武生習教之菏澤訓導宋璇，請卹擊匪陣歿之曹州學錄孔毓俊、生員孔毓仲，獎勵手擒賊渠之金鄉生員李九標。
units.en: That year sectarian rebels erupted in Huaxian and spread into Shandong; he impeached and dismissed Song Xuan, the Heze instructor, for failing to detect military licentiates practicing the sect; sought honors for Kong Yujun and licentiate Kong Yuzhong of Caozhou, who died fighting the rebels; and rewarded Jinxiang licentiate Li Jiubiao for capturing a rebel leader.
units.literal: That year, heterodox sect rebels rose in Huaxian and spread into Shandong; he impeached and dismissed Song Xuan, instructor of Heze, a military licentiate who had joined the sect and whose negligence went undetected; requested posthumous honors for Kong Yujun, recorder of Caozhou, and licentiate Kong Yuzhong, who died fighting the rebels; and rewarded Li Jiubiao, licentiate of Jinxiang, who personally captured the rebel chieftain.

units.zh: 十九年，召回京，仍內直，擢戶部侍郎，尋調禮部。
units.en: In Jiaqing 19 he was recalled to Beijing, resumed inner-court duty, became Vice Minister of Revenue, and was soon transferred to Rites.
units.literal: In the nineteenth year, recalled to the capital, still on inner-court duty, promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue, soon transferred to the Ministry of Rites.

units.zh: 充秘殿珠林、石渠寶笈續編總閱、全唐文館總裁，書成，並邀賞賚。
units.en: He served as chief reviewer for continued volumes of the imperial art catalogues and as director of the Complete Tang Prose project; when each was finished he received imperial rewards.
units.literal: He served as chief reviewer of the continued compilation of the Midian Zhulin and Shiqu Baoji and as director-general of the Complete Tang Prose Project; when the books were completed, he received rewards in both cases.

units.zh: 復調戶部。
units.en: He was transferred back to Revenue.
units.literal: Again transferred to the Board of Revenue.

units.zh: 二十四年，擢禮部尚書，加太子少保。
units.en: In Jiaqing 24 he became Minister of Rites and received the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, promoted to Minister of Rites and given the added title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 二十五年，命為軍機大臣，尋調戶部尚書。
units.en: In Jiaqing 25 he was appointed Grand Councillor and soon became Minister of Revenue.
units.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, appointed Grand Councillor, soon transferred to Minister of Revenue.

units.zh: 鉞受仁宗特達之知，久直內廷，書畫並被宸賞。
units.en: Yue enjoyed the Jiaqing Emperor's special favor; he served long in the inner court, and both his calligraphy and painting won imperial praise.
units.literal: Yue received the Jiaqing Emperor's exceptional personal recognition; he served long in the inner court, and both his calligraphy and painting received imperial appreciation.

units.zh: 習於掌故，持議詳慎。
units.en: Well versed in court precedent, he deliberated with care and thoroughness.
units.literal: Skilled in institutional precedent, he was detailed and cautious in deliberation.

units.zh: 宣宗即位，始畀樞務，甚優禮之。
units.en: When the Daoguang Emperor acceded, Yue was first given a seat on the Grand Council and treated with great deference.
units.literal: When the Xuanzong Emperor ascended the throne, he was first given Grand Council duties and was treated with great courtesy.

units.zh: 道光四年，以年老罷直軍機。
units.en: In Daoguang 4 he left the Grand Council on grounds of age.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Daoguang, because of age he was relieved of Grand Council duty.

units.zh: 累疏乞休，六年，始許致仕，在籍食半俸。
units.en: He repeatedly petitioned to retire; in Daoguang 6 he was finally allowed to do so and received half pay at home.
units.literal: He repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement; in the sixth year, retirement was finally granted, and he received half salary while at home.

units.zh: 二十一年，卒，年九十二，贈太子太保，諡勤敏。
units.en: He died in Daoguang 21 at ninety-two, was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and received the posthumous title Qinmin.
units.literal: In the twenty-first year, he died at age ninety-two; posthumously given the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; posthumous title Qinmin.

units.zh: 論曰：國家優禮詞臣，迴翔禁近，坐致公卿。
units.en: The commentators observe: The state honors literary officials; service near the throne readily leads to the highest offices.
units.literal: The commentary says: The state treats literary officials with favor; they move within the forbidden precincts and attain the rank of high minister without effort.

units.zh: 沈初、金士松，高宗舊臣，獲恩禮終。
units.en: Shen Chu and Jin Shisong, veterans of the Qianlong reign, enjoyed imperial favor to the end of their lives.
units.literal: Shen Chu and Jin Shisong were old ministers of the Gaozong Emperor and received imperial favor to the end.

units.zh: 王懿修父子同朝，尤稱盛事。
units.en: Wang Yixiu and his son serving together at court was especially celebrated.
units.literal: Wang Yixiu and his son serving in the same court was especially hailed as a grand occasion.

units.zh: 黃鉞以不附和珅，特邀殊遇，改授館職，馴參機務。
units.en: Huang Yue, for refusing to follow Heshen, won special favor, was transferred to Hanlin service, and eventually joined the Grand Council.
units.literal: Huang Yue, because he did not attach himself to Heshen, received special extraordinary favor, was transferred to Hanlin posts, and steadily participated in council affairs.

units.zh: 鄒炳泰、戴聯奎皆有耿介之操，晚節枯菀乃殊，要不失為端人焉。
units.en: Zou Bingtai and Dai Liankui were both men of upright character; their late careers ended differently, yet both remained men of integrity.
units.literal: Zou Bingtai and Dai Liankui both had upright and unyielding character; their late years withered or flourished differently, but in the end neither failed to be a man of integrity.
